messages:
Maria C: Quick heads-up — I rolled Ballast-6B (int4 per-tensor) to staging with micro-batching enabled. Getting a ~6% drop in recall@10 on our long-tail queries compared to fp16 baseline. :frowning:
Alex P: Hmm, interesting. Is the drop uniform across k or focused on long-tail only?
Maria C: Mostly long-tail (tail queries from our 10k holdout). recall@1/5 fine, but @10 and @50 degrade.
Sunil R: Could be KV-cache alignment or batching changing effective context windows. What batch sizes are you using?
Maria C: Default micro-batch size 8, global batch 256. Also enabled prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes.
Jen L: Any difference in embedding norms / cosine distribution? UMAP looked slightly more diffuse for tail points when I eyeballed it.
Maria C: Yes saw a small shift in L2 norms — mean norm down ~0.02. Cluster tightness lower on UMAP.
Alex P: Can you paste the eval command + exact metric numbers?
Maria C: Sure:
```
./eval_embeddings --model ballast-6b-int4 --holdout tail_holdout.jsonl --k 10 --batch-size 256 --microbatch 8 --kv-cache true
Recall@10: fp16=0.412  int4=0.387  delta=-0.025 (~6.1%)
```
Sunil R: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) quantization bias interacting with prefix kv-cache causing drift; 2) micro-batching causing different effective temperature / pooling due to request aggregation.
Jen L: Also check faiss index search params — were the index/w vectors rebuilt after int4 onboarding? Sometimes subtle float->quant mismatch if we reuse an old index.
Maria C: Index was rebuilt on int4 vectors (same pipeline). I can re-run with KV-cache off and with microbatch=1 to isolate.
OpsBot: Deploy log: ballast-6b-int4 staging deploy finished @4278912352 (pods=6, batch_worker=4).
Alex P: If microbatch=1 fixes it, that points to batching aggregation. If kv-cache off fixes it, then kv cache handling differs between fp16 and int4. Either way, let's run these 3 quick checks: (A) microbatch=1, (B) kv-cache=false, (C) rebuild index with fp16 vectors and search against int4 to see asymmetry.
Maria C: Kicking off A and B now. ETA ~20m. Will post plots (recall curve + norm hist) once done.
Sunil R: Also add a short ablation: run with per-channel quant (if available) — many models do better on long-tail with per-channel than per-tensor.
Maria C: Good call — I'll queue per-channel after these two.
Jen L: If we confirm it's kv-cache interaction, we may need a small calibration pass on cached keys post-quant to adjust scales. Not ideal but possible.
Maria C: Update: microbatch=1 restores recall@10 to within 0.5% of fp16. kv-cache=false still shows the drop.
Alex P: That screams micro-batching side-effect. Maybe the batching pipeline applies an extra normalization or averaging that quantized vectors are more sensitive to. Any non-deterministic ops in the pooling?
Maria C: I dug in — the micro-batcher applies a fused layernorm on aggregated token outputs before pooling (to reduce variance). Looks like the fused kernel behaves slightly differently under int4 path.
Sunil R: Let's try: (1) disable the fused layernorm in micro-batcher for int4 path, (2) run microbatch=8 with that change. If recall recovers we're done.
Maria C: Will test both. If that fixes it, we should add a unit test asserting recall parity on a short long-tail set when toggling microbatching kernels.
Alex P: Agreed. Also add a small note in the quant onboarding checklist: "verify micro-batch kernels + fused ops parity vs fp baseline".
Maria C: Tests running, sharing results in ~30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
